newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: A scramble for South African gold shares ensued during the afternoon as the bullion price rose from three-year lows touched on Tuesday and as the rand continued to weaken.

Dealers said there was strong local and foreign interest in gold stocks, helped by perceptions that recent sales, which on Tuesday saw the index fall to its lowest level in 11 months, had been overdone.
"The gold price is up and the rand is weaker. These two factors are working together positively for gold shares. There has been some good demand," a dealer said.
As the rand weakens against the dollar, the rand gold price increases.
Another said: "There has been some serious trade in golds. They have been so oversold that people feel they have to come for them."

The gold index added 1.6 percent or 24.1 points to 1,516.5 boosted by a 925 cent jump in Vaal Reefs to 329 rand, a 50 cent increase in Loraine to 14.50 and a 90 cent improvement in Freegold stock to 35 rand.
Traders said gold shares were seen continuing firmer on Thursday especially if bullion was able to hold its current $371 level, after rising off a $368 low earlier in the day.
Industrial shares ended weak for the third consecutive day on Wednesday amid a general lack of direction and a softer rand which ended the day at 4.66 against the dollar.
Dealers said a 79-point overnight loss on Wall Street, its biggest fall since July, had initially hindered stocks.
However, others said the South African market had not looked to the U.S. market for direction for many months. They blamed the 23.1 point fall in the index on a lack of direction.
The index ended at 7,968.6. The overall market index was 14.1 points firmer at 6,713.6.
On the futures market industrial contracts remained weaker on the day after initially being depressed by the fall on Wall Street. Golds perked up in tandem with bullion.
The industrial contract was at 1430 GMT seen at 7,721/33 from 7,751, the gold contract at 1,065/70 from 1,046 and the all share contract at 6,155/6,170 from 6,160.
